title: Central Bank Plans Fresh Foreign-Currency Injection as Dinar's Parallel Rate Slides to LYD 9.65/USD
detail: A Central Bank of Libya (CBL) source told Libya Herald the bank plans to inject additional foreign currency into the market 'over the coming days' after the dinar's black-market rate slipped to LYD 9.65 per US dollar — well above Governor Naji Issa's publicly stated target of holding the parallel-market gap within 5% of the official rate (under roughly LYD 7.00/USD). The source linked the move to 'improvements in various economic indicators and oil revenues, coinciding with understandings and agreements reached with economic partners,' and said the CBL aims to keep foreign reserves adequate for monetary stability while holding the fiscal deficit within year-end limits. No injection amount was specified. CBL Monetary Policy Committee member Ayoub Al-Farsi separately acknowledged, at the Sep 7–9 Arab Savings and Financial Literacy Conference in Tripoli, that two prior rounds of reference-rate revisions and currency injections this year had failed to close the gap with the black market.

media.caption: Central Bank of Libya headquarters; the CBL said it plans a fresh foreign-currency injection after the dinar's parallel rate hit LYD 9.65/USD, Sep 20, 2026

confidenceReason: Reported directly by Libya Herald citing a named-role CBL source; single-outlet report without independent corroboration of the exact 9.65 figure, though it is consistent with the CBL's own repeated public acknowledgment (via Al-Farsi) that the parallel-market gap has continued to widen through September.

title: MSF's Oyvon Rescues 31 Migrants as Libyan Patrol Boats Reportedly Burn the Empty Vessel at the Scene
detail: Médecins Sans Frontières said its rescue ship Oyvon pulled 31 people — including 6 women and girls and 12 minors, 9 of them unaccompanied, most from Eritrea — from a boat in distress in the central Mediterranean on Sunday, September 20, 2026. After everyone was safely aboard the Oyvon, the crew reported seeing Libyan patrol vessels arrive at the scene and set the now-empty migrant boat on fire. MSF project coordinator Chiara Milanese said 'we feared people would be pushed back to Libya,' where 'people rescued at sea should not be returned... [given] very serious risks including extortion, arbitrary detention, violence, and exploitation.' Italian authorities assigned Catania, Sicily as the disembarkation port. Libyan authorities did not comment on the incident.

media.caption: MSF's Oyvon rescues 31 migrants, mostly from Eritrea, in the central Mediterranean; crew reported Libyan patrol boats burned the empty migrant vessel afterward, Sep 20, 2026

confidenceReason: The rescue count, demographics, and Milanese's quotes are reported directly by InfoMigrants from MSF's own statement, independently corroborated by La Sicilia's report of the same Oyvon rescue and the burning of the empty boat; neither outlet identifies the specific Libyan patrol unit responsible.
